artists.biography:
Michelle David is an American soul and gospel singer born on August 28, 1966, in Winston-Salem, North Carolina. Raised in New York from age ten, she began her musical journey in church at just four years old and joined her first gospel group, The Mission of Love, at age five. Throughout the 1980s and 1990s, David built an impressive career performing in Broadway productions including Mama, I Want To Sing, The Sound of Motown, Glory of Gospel, and Mahalia, while also contributing background vocals for legendary artists Diana Ross and Michael Bolton. Her early training at the Fame School of Performing Arts and her deep roots in gospel music shaped her distinctive vocal style and artistic sensibility.

Since relocating to the Netherlands in 1994, David has established herself as a contemporary soul powerhouse. In 2015, she formed Michelle David & The True-tones with guitarist Paul Willemsen, bassist Onno Smit, and drummer Bas Bouma, releasing seven critically acclaimed albums that blend traditional gospel with modern soul, funk, rock, and afro-beat influences. The group's innovative approach to gospel—infusing classic ecclesiastic pieces with contemporary arrangements and diverse musical inspirations—has earned them an Edison nomination and established them as a must-see live act. They have performed at major European festivals including Pinkpop and North Sea Jazz, toured extensively across Europe and beyond, and even performed at the 2022 Winter Olympics.

David's artistry is defined by her powerful vocals, emotional depth, and willingness to push gospel music into fresh sonic territories. With The True-tones, she has created a distinctive sound characterized by groovy basslines, upbeat grooves, and strong melodies that resonate with audiences worldwide. Her work represents a pioneering approach to contemporary gospel, honoring tradition while embracing modern influences and creating an authentic musical experience that transcends generational boundaries.

artists.biography:
Michelle David & The True-Tones is a Dutch soul band featuring American vocalist Michelle David, raised in New York where she began singing gospel in church at age four and performed with The Mission of Love by five. After touring globally with Broadway productions like Mama, The Sound of Motown, Glory of Gospel, and Mahalia, and recording with artists such as Diana Ross and Michael Bolton, she settled in the Netherlands. There, she teamed up with Dutch musicians Paul Willemsen (guitar, bass), Onno Smit (guitar, bass), and Bas Bouma (drums), initially as a project exploring gospel roots of rhythm & blues and soul, evolving into a tight-knit band blending gospel, soul, blues, jazz, afrobeat, and more.

The band's sound is defined by groovy basslines, powerhouse vocals, and a fusion of classic soul with contemporary and global influences like Afrofunk, Calypso, Moroccan Gnawa, Brazilian flavors, and 70s indie vibes, earning them acclaim as one of Europe's most dynamic live acts. They have released at least seven critically acclaimed albums, including gospel-infused works, a Christmas album, Brothers & Sisters, and Truth & Soul (2022), with honors like a Dutch Edison Award nomination, BBC Radio 6 Album of the Year, and FIP Radio Album of the Month.

Their significance lies in reinventing gospel and soul traditions into vibrant, empowering spectacles, headlining festivals like Pinkpop, North Sea Jazz, and Veszprém Blues, performing at the 2022 Winter Olympics, and selling out shows worldwide, all while overcoming personal challenges like Michelle David's breast cancer diagnosis to continue trailblazing as "Holland's best soul singer.

perplexity.description:
Michelle David & The True-Tones' Soul Woman, released February 27, 2026, on Record Kicks, represents a pivotal inward turn for the US-Dutch gospel-soul ensemble following the outward-facing critical success of their 2024 debut with the label, Brothers & Sisters. This 10-track album, clocking in at 38 minutes, delves deeply into themes of personal identity, healing, and spiritual resilience, as Michelle David reflects: “How can I ask others to take time to reflect on their lives if I’m not doing the same myself?” Centered on David's raw, warm, and purposeful voice—honed from childhood singing, Broadway credits, and collaborations with icons like Diana Ross and Michael Bolton—the record blends gospel fire with vintage rhythm & blues, evoking Curtis Mayfield's introspection, Bobby Womack's grit, The Blind Boys of Alabama's fervor, and the joyous uplift of Diana Ross & The Supremes.

Musically, Soul Woman refines the band's retro-soul signature through analog-driven arrangements by longtime collaborators Paul Willemsen (guitar, bass), Onno Smit (guitar, bass), and Bas Bouma (drums), incorporating (Northern) soul stompers like the single "Running" and the lead track "Speak To Me." Available on LP (including clear and transparent vinyl editions), CD, and digital, it builds on the group's acclaimed discography—including the Edison-nominated The Gospel Sessions, BBC Radio 6's Album of the Year Truth & Soul (2020), and festival triumphs at Pinkpop and North Sea Jazz—positioning them at the forefront of modern retro soul with timeless grooves and urgent authenticity.

The album's reception underscores its significance in the funk/soul revival, earning early plays on stations like WNCW and praise for its gravity and sparkle amid International Women’s Month celebrations, cementing Michelle David & The True-Tones' legacy of heartfelt, boundary-pushing gospel-soul.
